solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Run off to get married? Outside Italy that's allowed

indicators.note: the two pieces for running off and marrying are placed around the letter for Italy

parts.note: to leg it is slang for running away
to mate is to pair up, an old sense of marrying
I is the international vehicle code for Italy

explanation.surface: An eloping couple wonders whether a wedding held beyond Italy's borders would be lawful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Run off to get married' suggests ELOPE, but it splits into LEG IT and MATE, which go 'Outside' I.
explanation.definitionFit: Something legitimate is lawful or permitted, which is what allowed means here.

clue.text: Penniless Yank makes fortune

indicators.note: without a penny, so the letter P, short for penny, is taken away

parts.note: to yank is to pull sharply, to pluck

explanation.surface: A broke American somehow strikes it rich.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Yank' looks like an American but is the verb, PLUCK; 'Penniless' removes its P (penny).
explanation.definitionFit: Luck and fortune are synonyms for chance, good or bad, that shapes events.

clue.text: Perhaps shift manager, losing article carelessly, gets tense

indicators.note: done carelessly, the remaining letters are thrown into a new order
the word manager loses one of its letters, the article

parts.note: A is the indefinite article
T is the standard grammar abbreviation for tense

explanation.surface: A manager who perhaps works shifts sloppily drops things and grows anxious.
explanation.walkthrough: Only one A of the two is lost, and 'carelessly' then works on the six letters left; a shift is a simple loose dress.
explanation.definitionFit: A shift is a loose dress, so it is an example of an item of clothing; 'Perhaps' marks the example.

clue.text: Forcibly remove item of sports outfit as reprimand

definitions.text: Forcibly remove item of sports outfit
definitions.meaning: taken literally, to rip off a piece of a team's kit, the strip being a team's playing outfit
the idiom means to scold someone severely

explanation.surface: An angry coach rips a player's kit as a rebuke.
explanation.walkthrough: In British usage a team's STRIP is its kit, so the phrase literally describes ripping a piece of kit away.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom is British slang for scolding someone fiercely, a severe telling-off.

clue.text: Swampy's mother runs to join cast

parts.note: ma is an informal word for mother
R is the cricket scoring abbreviation for runs
to shy is to throw, as at a coconut shy

explanation.surface: An eco-protester's mother joins the cast of a play.
explanation.walkthrough: Swampy was a well-known British road protester, so the surface reads as a person's name; it is the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Marshy ground is boggy and waterlogged, a synonym for swampy.

clue.text: Macbeth's territory compared with Esau's

parts.note: than is the word used in comparisons
in Genesis Esau is the ancestor of the Edomites, so Edom is his land

explanation.surface: A comparison of the realms of Shakespeare's Macbeth and the biblical Esau.
explanation.definitionFit: Macbeth was Thane of Glamis and Cawdor; a thane's domain or rank is his territory.

clue.text: No work for cop in nick

indicators.note: no work, with something given for it, means the letters for work are swapped out for another piece
no work, with something given for it, means the letters for work are swapped out for another piece

parts.note: taken as written
OP is short for opus, a work
in, meaning fashionable, is hip

explanation.surface: A police officer with no work to do sits in a prison cell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nick' looks like prison slang but is the definition; 'in' is no container indicator but means trendy, which takes the place of the work.
explanation.definitionFit: A chip is a small notch or flaw in a surface, the same as a nick.

clue.text: A bit of a shock south of the border, discovering poison

indicators.note: in a down answer the piece written lower comes after the one above it

parts.note: a hem is the border of a piece of cloth
a lock is a tuft taken from a shock, a thick mass of hair

explanation.surface: Someone gets a nasty surprise south of the border on finding poison.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shock' suggests surprise but means a mass of hair, of which a LOCK is a bit; 'the border' is a hem, not a frontier.
explanation.definitionFit: Hemlock is a plant whose extract is a famous poison, used to execute Socrates.

clue.text: Senior persons? Not right, so different term for older folk

indicators.note: made different, the remaining letters are put into a fresh order
not having these letters means they are taken out of the two words

explanation.surface: A writer seeks a fresh label for elderly people, since the current one seems wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not' takes R and SO out of SENIORPERSONS, leaving ENIOPERSNS, which 'different' rearranges; 'term for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Pensioners are people drawing a retirement income, usually elderly people.

clue.text: Pirate gold's hidden in heap of stones, mostly

indicators.note: hidden in means put inside the other piece
mostly means all but the last letter is kept

parts.note: a cairn is a mound of stones built as a marker
OR is gold in heraldry, with the S from the possessive

explanation.surface: A pirate's treasure has been buried under a pile of rocks.
explanation.walkthrough: OR is gold in heraldry; the 's supplies the S rather than meaning 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A corsair was a privateer or pirate, especially of the Barbary coast.

clue.text: Belly dancing half-heartedly banned to keep order

indicators.note: the rearranged letters keep, or hold, the order piece inside
dancing letters move about into a new arrangement
the heart of the word banned is its double N, and half of that is dropped

parts.note: OM is the Order of Merit

explanation.surface: Belly dancing, done without enthusiasm, has been banned to keep public order.
explanation.walkthrough: The heart of the word is its double N, so 'half-heartedly' drops just one; 'dancing' gives ABDEN, which keeps the order inside.
explanation.definitionFit: The abdomen is the stomach area of the body, informally the belly.

clue.text: Is every one of the male pupils taking heroin? That's a bad school

indicators.note: the question takes the heroin letter into itself

parts.words: Is every one of the male pupils
parts.note: the question can be rephrased as 'do the boys all?'
H is slang for heroin

explanation.surface: A worried parent asks whether all the boys at a school are on heroin.
explanation.walkthrough: The school is the brutal Yorkshire academy run by Wackford Squeers in Dickens's Nicholas Nickleby.
explanation.definitionFit: Dickens's fictional boarding school is a byword for cruelty and neglect of pupils.

clue.text: Reserve or several reserves?

definitions.meaning: reserve as a trait is aloofness or emotional distance
a body of troops detailed for a separate task is a unit of several soldiers

explanation.surface: A puzzled query about whether a word means a reserve or several of them.
explanation.definitionFit: The answer means both emotional aloofness and a body of troops sent off separately.

clue.text: Old boy's current fetish

parts.note: OB is the abbreviation for old boy, a former pupil
I is the physics symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: A former pupil's present-day obsession.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fetish' suggests an obsession but means a magical charm here.
explanation.definitionFit: Obi, also obeah, is a West Indian form of sorcery or a charm used in it, a fetish object.

clue.text: Clue for "rain" is restored

parts.note: rein, when stated or spoken, sounds like the word rain, so the two pieces make a clue for that word

explanation.surface: A setter explains that a clue for the word rain has been put back.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as REIN STATED the answer is itself a homophone clue leading to 'rain'; 'Clue for' and 'is' are links, and read whole the answer means restored.
explanation.definitionFit: Reinstated means put back in a former position, a synonym for restored.

clue.text: Being who I am, I had to leave

indicators.note: the shortened form for I had must leave the longer word

parts.note: your identity is who you are
I'd is the contraction of I had

explanation.surface: Someone explains who they are and that they had to go.
explanation.definitionFit: An entity is a thing with distinct existence, which is what a being is.

clue.text: Russian military leader gives a lot of money to family? About half of them

parts.note: a pot, or pots, of money is a large sum

indicators.note: the second half of the word them is taken

parts.note: kin are your relatives

explanation.surface: A Russian commander hands a fortune to his relatives, or about half of them.
explanation.walkthrough: Grigory Potemkin was Catherine the Great's general and favourite.
explanation.definitionFit: Potemkin was an eighteenth-century Russian field marshal and statesman.

clue.text: After short look old chap ordered soup

indicators.note: the anagram comes after the short look in the answer
short means the last letter is cut off

parts.note: to gaze is to look steadily

indicators.note: ordered means put into a new order

explanation.surface: An old man glances at the menu and orders soup.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ordered' looks like ordering food but means rearrange O and CHAP into PACHO.
explanation.definitionFit: Gazpacho is a cold Spanish soup of tomatoes and vegetables.

clue.text: Reported bad state of ships

indicators.note: reported means the pieces are as spoken, giving a word that sounds like them

parts.note: naughty means badly behaved; to call is to state or declare

explanation.surface: A news item on the poor condition of a fleet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'state' looks like a noun (condition) but is the verb, CALL.
explanation.definitionFit: Nautical means relating to ships, sailors or navigation.

clue.text: At university degree is to improve

parts.note: up means in residence at university, as in up at Oxford
a grade is a degree or level

explanation.surface: A student says a university degree is the way to get on.
explanation.definitionFit: To upgrade is to raise to a higher standard, so to make better.

clue.text: One buys second discounted jumper

indicators.note: discounted means taken off, so the letter for second is removed

parts.note: a shopper is someone who buys

explanation.surface: A customer buys a reduced-price second-hand sweater.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jumper' is British for a sweater, which suits the shopping surface, but here it means something that jumps.
explanation.definitionFit: A hopper is anything that hops, such as an insect, so it is a jumper.

clue.text: Tom's sister concealing love for him?

parts.note: tom is British slang for a prostitute, a pro

indicators.note: the sister word conceals the love letter inside it

parts.note: a nun is a religious sister
love is zero in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: A girl hides her love for a boy from her brother Tom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tom' looks like a name but is slang for a prostitute (PRO). 'him?' is an example of the answer, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Him is an example of a word standing in for a noun, here the objective form of he.

clue.text: Spiritual movement created by Sunderland workers' pay?

parts.note: Sunderland is a city in north-east England, NE
a wage is what workers are paid

explanation.surface: A spiritual revival prompted by how much Sunderland's workers earn.
explanation.definitionFit: New Age is a loose spiritual movement drawing on alternative and mystical beliefs.

clue.text: Retired gun dog

indicators.note: retired means drawn back, so the gun word is read backwards

parts.note: gat is old slang for a gun

explanation.surface: A gundog that has stopped working.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gun dog' reads as one breed; split it: 'dog' is the verb meaning follow.
explanation.definitionFit: To tag along behind someone is to follow them closely, to dog them.

clue.text: Person is beaten up after opposing parliament's leaders, exemplifying this?

definitions.text: Person is beaten up after opposing parliament's leaders, exemplifying this?

indicators.note: the anagram is placed after those first letters
the leaders of the two words are their first letters
beaten up means knocked about into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A dissident is assaulted for opposing the heads of parliament, an example of state tyranny.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beaten up' turns PERSONIS into PRESSION.
explanation.definitionFit: Oppression is cruel or unjust treatment by those in power, which a beating for dissent illustrates.

clue.text: Thchoolgirl'th a legend

indicators.note: the possessive written as th shows the speaker lisps, so the schoolgirl word is said with a lisp

parts.note: a miss is a schoolgirl, as pupils address a teacher

explanation.surface: A lisping schoolgirl talks about a legend.
explanation.walkthrough: With the lisp the clue spells out, a miss is pronounced like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A myth is a traditional story of gods or heroes, much like a legend.

clue.text: In court one fellow very much rebutted dishonest trading

indicators.note: rebutted, pushed back, means the whole assembled string is read backwards
the three short pieces go in the court abbreviation

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
far means very much, as in far better

explanation.surface: In court, a man flatly denies a charge of crooked dealing.
explanation.walkthrough: I, F and FAR go In CT to make CIFFART, which rebutted turns backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To traffic in goods is to deal in them illegally, as in drug trafficking.

clue.text: Loving laconic statement by right- winger?

indicators.note: laconic means terse, so the opening I of the statement is dropped

parts.note: a right-winger might declare 'I am a Tory', a member of Britain's Conservative Party

explanation.surface: A Conservative's affectionate but terse declaration.
explanation.walkthrough: A Tory is a member of Britain's right-wing Conservative Party.
explanation.definitionFit: Amatory means concerned with love or desire, so it means loving.

clue.text: Long time to go without sugar perhaps

parts.note: to be dying for something is to long for it

explanation.surface: It is a long time to give up sugar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Long' looks like an adjective but is the verb, as in dying for a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: To diet is to restrict what you eat, such as cutting out sugar.

clue.text: Business meeting's to lessen blow when leaders exchange positions

indicators.note: the leading letters of the two words swap places

parts.note: to lower is to reduce
a punch is a blow

explanation.surface: Advice that a business meeting reduces a blow if its leaders trade places.
explanation.definitionFit: A power lunch is a midday meal where executives do business.
